combined_conclusion: For n in {9,15}, a>=2 and b,c>=1, no pairwise-coprime positive integers solve a coefficient-one generalized Fermat equation whose exponent multiset is {2a,3b,nc}.
conditional_n11_extension: Using the GRH-conditional Freitas-Naskrecki-Stoll classification gives the analogous {2a,3b,11c} family; certifying five degree-36 class groups would make that instance unconditional.

n15.conclusion: no primitive positive coefficient-one equation with exponent multiset {2a,3b,15c} exists for a>=2,b,c>=1

n9.conclusion: no primitive positive coefficient-one equation with exponent multiset {2a,3b,9c} exists for a>=2,b,c>=1

nonclaim: The replay verifies the exact displayed solution lists, equations, primitivity, sign filters, and valuation-one obstructions. Completeness of each list is imported from the cited peer-reviewed theorem.
relationship_to_existing_n7_result: The same transfer principle recovers the previously certified {2a,3b,7c} family from Poonen-Schaefer-Stoll.

transfer_principle.criterion: in every classified row compatible with one of the three sign patterns, the positive x-coordinate is not a proper power
transfer_principle.permutation_coverage: the three choices of right-hand exponent, together with swapping the two positive summands, cover all six permutations
transfer_principle.scope: odd n and a complete primitive-integer classification of x^2+y^3=z^n
